previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for her third cycle of R-ICE chemotherapy for EBV-positive classical Hodgkin lymphoma with skull base and nasopharyngeal involvement, following a good response after two prior cycles. She tolerated treatment with mild somnolence from ifosfamide, which resolved, and required a single unit of packed red blood cells due to anemia. Her white blood cell and platelet counts remained low but stable, without infection. An MRI showed continued regression of the skull base mass with no new intracranial lesions. She was discharged home with instructions to start filgrastim, monitor blood glucose due to steroid-induced hyperglycemia, and follow up for blood counts and transplant evaluation. Her chronic conditions, including CVID, diabetes, and back pain, were managed throughout.

Ms. ___ is a ___ year old woman with a past medical history 
significant for CVID, type 2 DM, asthma, large cell lymphoma

ACUTE ISSUES

# C.Diff/Colitis: GI performed a flexible sigmoidoscopy, which 
revealed proctitis (consistent with CT A/P). DDx includes 
infection (including CMV, bacterial, etc) or diversion colitis 
related to colostomy. Biopsies were negative for CMV.  Stool 
studies returned showing C.Diff. There were no pseudomembranes 
on sigmoidoscopy. Patient started on PO and PR vanco. Given 
neutropenia, PR vanco was discontinued. Biopsies showed chronic 
severe colitis (absence of lamina propria plasma cells 
consistent with CVI). Rectal c.diff was negative. Patient given 
rectal enema of mesalamine on ___ with good efficacy, 
however they were stopped due to neutropenia. Patient had 
recurrent abdominal pain on ___ after stopping the enemas. This 
was presumed to be seconary to mucositis as there were mucositic 
ulcers on the mouth and on the ileostomy. A 14 day course of 
flagyl was completed and the patient was discharged on PO vanc 
to continue until readmission for transplant.

# Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma: Now s/p 3 cycles of R-ICE.  Continued 
Filgrastim 400 mg SC daily, HSV prophylaxis with acyclovir 400 
mg q8h, PCP ___ with ___ 1500 mg daily. Plan is 
for patient to return next week for stem cell transplant. She 
was cleared by dental. ID pre-allo eval seen ___, rec urine 
histo Ag, strongyloides Ab, which were sent. Head MRI for 
staging is done and shows interval improvement in her CNS 
disease.
 
# Anemia: Past has a history of iron-deficiency anemia. She 
received 4 units of PRBCs this admission. There was one further 
episode of rectal bleeding when platelets were down to 11. This 
resolved after platelet transfusion.  

# Type 2 DM, uncontrolled: On glimepiride and metformin as 
outpatient. Orals stopped no admission and switched to ISS. 
After administration of IVIG and stopping oral hypoglycemics, 
patient's FSBG increased to greater than 400. The patient was 
severely insulin resistant, requiring extremely high doses of 
insulin without good control. It is possible that the patient 
has antibodies against exogenous insulin, which were amplified 
after giving IVIG. Metformin was restarted. Sugars have 
improved, but remain elevated. Adjusted to diabetic diet with 
disconitnuation of high carb supplements and replacement with 
benecalorie supplement per ___ recommendation. 
Sugars improved significantly with these changes. Patient had 
symptomatic low to 72 and regimen was adjusted accordingly.

and lyrica were continued. She occasionally required IV dilaudid

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with history of lymphoma with enhancing
nasopharyngeal mass. Please re-evaluate and compare to prior study.

TECHNIQUE:  Sagittal T1 weighted, axial diffusion weighted, and axial FLAIR
images of the brain were obtained. Axial T1 weighted and fat-suppressed T2
weighted images of the nasopharynx, and coronal STIR images of the nasopharynx
were obtained. Following intravenous gadolinium administration, fat-suppressed
axial T1 weighted images of the nasopharynx, coronal T1 weighted images of the
nasopharynx, and axial T1 weighted images of the entire brain were obtained.

COMPARISON:  ___ and ___ MRIs.

FINDINGS: 

The right skullbase mass centered within the nasopharynx has progressively
decreased in size compared to ___ and ___. The associated
contrast enhancement has markedly decreased. The right nasopharyngeal and
oropharyngeal tissues remain slightly thickened compared to the left. There is
continued involvement of the right foramen ovale and decreased, but not
completely resolved dural enhancement along the inferior right temporal lobe.

Right level 2 lymph nodes demonstrates progressive decrease in size, with the
largest node now measuring 12 x 9 mm (with an normal limits) compared to 19 x
14 mm on ___.

No pathologic contrast enhancement is seen in the brain parenchyma. Again seen
is encephalomalacia in the inferior left parietal lobe, consistent with
postsurgical change given the adjacent craniotomy, with stable adjacent high
signal on FLAIR images without mass effect. Scattered small foci of high
signal on FLAIR images in the subcortical, deep, and periventricular white
matter of the cerebral hemispheres are unchanged, nonspecific but compatible
with sequela of mild chronic small vessel ischemic disease or prior
inflammation. There is no acute infarction. The ventricles are stable in size.
The body, atrium, and occipital horn of the left lateral ventricle remain
larger than the right.

Sagittal T1 weighted images again demonstrate high signal in the basal
ganglia, which may be seen secondary to chronic liver disease or TPN, as well
as in the setting of neurofibromatosis type 1.

The orbits appear unremarkable without evidence for a mass for inflammatory
change.

Right mastoid air cells remain partially opacified.

IMPRESSION:


1. The right skullbase mass centered in the nasopharynx has progressively
decreased in size compared to ___. Associated contrast
enhancement has markedly decreased, but right nasopharyngeal and oropharyngeal
soft tissues remain thickened.
2. Continued involvement of the right foramen ovale and decreased, but not
completely resolved dural enhancement along the inferior right temporal lobe.
3. Progressive decreased size of right level 2 lymph nodes.
4. Stable post treatment changes in the left inferior parietal lobe. No
evidence for a new lesion in the brain parenchyma.
